title: SpoC-128-DS
blurb: SpoC-128 with the nonce domain-separated from the mode controls. The published three-query key recovery cannot be addressed here. Whether anything else can is open.

scoring.exponent_rationale: Decision game: advantage a needs ~a^-2 repetitions to amplify to constant confidence, so q/a^2 is the cost of deciding. Search-flavoured challenges (key recovery, forgery) set 1. No default is baked in; see Micciancio-Walter, On the Bit Security of Cryptographic Primitives.
scoring.note: score = log2(budget / advantage^exponent), the security level in bits the attack refutes. Lower is better.

par.source: SpoC-128 key length, NIST LWC Round-2 specification
par.note: Par is the designer's own security claim. Under par is a break of the claim.

baseline.note: Exhaustive key search. The only thing on the frontier so far.

what_changed: The four mode-control bits (tag 0x80, plaintext 0x40, associated data 0x20, partial block 0x10) are reserved in the nonce: a legal nonce satisfies `n &&& 0xF0 = 0`. The mode itself is untouched.
why: `load key n` puts the nonce in the rate and `tagInput` XORs `tagControl` into the same rate, so `tagInput (load key n) = load key (n ^^^ tagControl)`. One permutation input was reachable by two queries, and since the permutation is public and invertible, half of it leaks in a tag and half in a ciphertext block. Reserving the control bits makes `n ^^^ tagControl` unaddressable.
not_claimed: That this variant is secure. Nobody has looked. Closing one published route into a mode is not an argument that no other route exists — which is why it is on the board.

comparison_points.name: SpoC-128 (unrestricted nonce)
comparison_points.caveats: The parent challenge, broken at 3 queries and advantage 1. Its attack needs nonce = 0x80, which is illegal here, so that score does not transfer.

score_source.note: Declared by the submission, in Lean. The Solution type is indexed by them, so they are part of what is proved; the verifier reads them back with #eval rather than parsing a form.
